title: Amaranthus: modeled ₹406/qtl left, Palayam → Madhavapuram
summary: January 2023: reported amaranthus prices at Palayam and Madhavapuram imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 92% of 24 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹406 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 86 same-variety market pairs screened for amaranthus in January 2023; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Madhavapuram report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2023
scenes.caption: Palayam (Kerala) and Madhavapuram (Kerala) both reported amaranthus prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 24 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Palayam reported a median ₹2,000 per quintal. Madhavapuram reported a median ₹2,600 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹700/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹700 per quintal, and Madhavapuram was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 287 km by road
scenes.caption: 287 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~5 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹62/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹388 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹237 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Madhavapuram report, the rule selects 22 of 24 modeled shipping days. 21 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹406 per quintal (₹257 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Amaranthus route from Palayam to Madhavapuram was positive on 92% of matched days in January 2023. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹40,600, or ₹25,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to amaranthus
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹62/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Amaranthus route from Palayam to Madhavapuram was positive on 92% of matched days in January 2023. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹40,600, or ₹25,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

title: Amaranthus: modeled ₹678/qtl left, Thalayolaparambu → Neyyatinkara
summary: November 2023: reported amaranthus prices at Thalayolaparambu and Neyyatinkara imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 19 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹678 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 92 same-variety market pairs screened for amaranthus in November 2023; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Neyyatinkara report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: November 2023
scenes.caption: Thalayolaparambu (Kerala) and Neyyatinkara (Kerala) both reported amaranthus prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 19 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Thalayolaparambu reported a median ₹2,600 per quintal. Neyyatinkara reported a median ₹3,700 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,000/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,000 per quintal, and Neyyatinkara was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 202 km by road
scenes.caption: 202 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~3 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹44/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹620 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹423 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Neyyatinkara report, the rule selects 19 of 19 modeled shipping days. 19 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹678 per quintal (₹482 under stress).
